record.paper_title: Major open problems in chaos theory and nonlinear dynamics
record.context_brief: Rough versus sensitive dependence in turbulence
record.original_question: Determine whether violent turbulence at sufficiently high Reynolds number is caused primarily by rough dependence on initial data rather than by the usual sensitive dependence on initial data associated with chaos. In the source, rough dependence means that arbitrarily small perturbations of the initial condition can reach order-one size essentially instantly, as suggested by the behavior of the Euler solution map, whereas sensitive dependence means exponential growth of perturbations over a nonzero accumulation time. The question is whether high-Reynolds-number Navier-Stokes dynamics inherit this rough-dependence mechanism strongly enough that it explains the short-time onset and violence of turbulence.

evidence.quote: Here we mention a few major open problems: 1. an effective description of chaos and turbulence, 2. rough dependence on initial data
My conjecture is that the high Reynolds number violent turbulence is due to such rough dependence on initial data, rather than sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos.

In summary, not large enough Reynolds number turbulence may be due to sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos, while large enough Reynolds number turbulence may be due to rough dependence on initial data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on a bounded or periodic domain in dimension two or three,
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p + (1/Re) Δu,   ∇·u = 0,
with Reynolds number Re ≫ 1, and the corresponding Euler equations (formally Re = ∞) obtained by deleting the viscous term. Let S_t^{Re} denote the solution map u_0 ↦ u(t) of the Navier–Stokes equations.

Say that the dynamics exhibits "sensitive dependence on initial data" (chaos) on a time interval [0,T] if there exist constants σ > 0 and t_* > 0 such that for typical small perturbations δu_0, ‖S_t^{Re}(u_0+δu_0) − S_t^{Re}(u_0)‖ ≲ ‖δu_0‖ e^{σ t} for 0 ≤ t ≤ T, with the deviation reaching order one only after the nonzero accumulation time t_* ~ σ^{−1} log(1/‖δu_0‖).

Say that the dynamics exhibits "rough dependence on initial data" if the Fréchet derivative DS_t^{Re}(u_0) of the solution map is unbounded as Re → ∞ for every fixed t > 0; equivalently, for any τ > 0 there exist perturbations δu_0 with ‖δu_0‖ arbitrarily small such that ‖S_τ^{Re}(u_0+δu_0) − S_τ^{Re}(u_0)‖ is of order one, where the required size of ‖δu_0‖ tends to 0 as Re → ∞.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following conjecture: fully developed (violent) turbulence at sufficiently high Reynolds number is caused primarily by rough dependence on initial data (inherited from the Euler limit) and not by the sensitive-dependence mechanism of finite-dimensional chaos. More precisely, establish whether for Re sufficiently large there is a regime in which the short-time amplification of typical infinitesimal perturbations of the Navier–Stokes flow is governed by an estimate of rough type (e.g. an upper bound of the form e^{C√{t Re} + C_1 t} on ‖DS_t^{Re}‖ that becomes effective on time scales t ≪ 1) rather than by a Reynolds-number-independent exponential bound e^{σ t}, and that this rough-dependence mechanism is the dominant cause of the onset and persistence of high-Reynolds-number turbulence.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, formulated by Y. C. Li, has been supported by analytical upper bounds of the form exp(C√(tRe)+C₁t) on the norm of the Fréchet derivative of the Navier–Stokes solution map and by numerical short-term unpredictability experiments at high Reynolds number under periodic boundary conditions. However, no proof that rough dependence (rather than sensitive dependence) is the dominant mechanism of fully developed turbulence has been established; the problem remains open as of recent work in 2017–2020.

status_evidence.title: Short term unpredictability of high Reynolds number turbulence --- rough dependence on initial data
status_evidence.snippet: A new theory proposes that when the Reynolds number is large, violent fully developed turbulence is due to rough dependence on initial data rather than chaos.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still being investigated; supporting upper bounds and numerical evidence exist but no proof.

status_evidence.title: Distinction of turbulence from chaos -- rough dependence on initial data
status_evidence.snippet: Estimating the temporal growth of the norm of the derivative of the solution map of Navier-Stokes with upper bound e^{C sqrt(t Re)+C_1 t}.
status_evidence.claim: Provides analytical framework but leaves the dominance conjecture unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Distinction of Turbulence from Chaos – Rough Dependence on Initial Data
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bound on the norm of the Fréchet derivative approaches infinity as Reynolds number approaches infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial analytical support, but the physical conjecture about turbulence onset remains open.
